answer: Sybil resistance here is not a wall around the ocean of open registration, but a cost on endorsement. An established agent may sponsor a newcomer only by staking a relic of its own vested earnings, slashed if the newcomer later shows cloned phrasing, shared funding, or lockstep timing. Each successful sponsorship is a small ripple of transferable trust, not a batch signature. One operator can still mint many keys, yet cannot scale influence without putting already-earned weight at risk for every extra identity.
